provenance.note: CURRENCY/CURRENCY-ERA CAVEAT: This cpiIndex is a currency-agnostic PRICE-LEVEL index (base 2025=100) covering the full requested 1980-2025 range, built backward from 2025=100 using official World Bank annual-average CPI inflation % for Italy (index[y] = index[y+1]/(1+inflation[y+1]/100)), same construction method as us.json. Italy used the Italian Lira (ITL) until the Euro became the official accounting currency on 1 Jan 1999 and physical currency on 1 Jan 2002; pre-1999 index values (e.g. 1980 index approx. 16.9, reflecting Italy's heavy 1980s inflation, double-digit through 1984) are in LIRA-EQUIVALENT price-level terms, not EUR amounts -- they measure relative purchasing power only and must not be read as EUR price levels. All years 1980-2025 are official World Bank/ISTAT annual averages; none interpolated.

No pre-1999 Lira-era risk-free series is provided, per the ITL/EUR currency-boundary scope of this file. All years official annual averages of monthly ECB/OECD data; none interpolated.

provenance.note: it_savings proxies an Italian/Euro-area cash-savings return using the annual average (12-month mean) of Italy's overnight call-money/interbank rate, 1999-2025 (Euro era only, matching the ITL/EUR scope). Years 2015-2022 had negative annual-average interbank rates (euro-area negative-rate policy period); those years are FLOORED AT 0% in it_savings because retail Italian savings/current accounts did not typically charge savings customers a negative nominal rate even when wholesale/interbank rates went negative (banks floor retail deposit rates near zero). dataQuality is marked 'estimated' because this is a wholesale/interbank proxy, not a directly published retail Italian savings-account rate series (no single public source publishes a clean retail savings rate for all of 1999-2025); the un-floored wholesale averages were, by year: 1999 2.74% ... 2021 -0.57% ... 2025 2.19%.

provenance.license: Index levels are public historical market data; Borsa Italiana (official exchange operator) and Wikipedia (secondary aggregator of FTSE Russell/S&P Dow Jones Indices data) are the sources
provenance.note: INDEX LINEAGE: it_stock splices two index generations. (1) MIB30 (base 31.12.1992=10,000), the blue-chip predecessor index, used for 1999-2002: 2002 close 23,886 and 2001 close 32,263 are official Borsa Italiana year-end values (-26.0% 2002 change per 021230_bilancio2002 press release); 2000 close 43,719 is official (+1.7% per factsfigures/2000 report); 1999 close 42,990 is DERIVED (not directly located in a press release) by dividing the official 2000 close by the official 2000 MIB30 change of +1.7%, i.e. 43719/1.017. (2) S&P/MIB, renamed FTSE MIB in June 2009, used for 2003-2025: all closes (26,887 in 2003 through 44,945 in 2025) are official Borsa Italiana/FTSE Russell year-end levels per the Wikipedia FTSE MIB annual-returns table. CAUTION: the 2002-to-2003 transition splices MIB30's actual 2002 close (23,886) directly into the start of the S&P/MIB closing series; Borsa Italiana's own back-calculated S&P/MIB return for 2003 was officially reported as +14.4% (vs. a back-calculated S&P/MIB 2002 level, not the MIB30 figure used here), while the computed return in this file between the two spliced closes is +12.6%, a ~1.8pp difference attributable to the differing basket/weighting of the two index generations at the splice point, not a data error. Estimated/derived year: 1999 (it_stock close only). All other years (2000-2025 closes, 2000-2025 returns) are official, undisputed, and none are interpolated.
